title: Trademark Prosecution in Practice
subtitle: Ten recorded sessions that take one mark from the first search to the hearing notice: search reports, risk calls, examination report responses and written submissions, drafted the way the Registry expects them.
summary: The complete prosecution cycle in ten two-hour sessions, all recorded. Half the course is the pre-filing search most juniors are never taught properly; the other half is the examination report, the written submission and the hearing. Ten practice exercises, email support throughout, and a community of IP professionals.
outcomes: Classify a proposed mark and predict its Section 9 and Section 11 exposure before anyone files
Build search strings that find phonetic, visual and transliterated variants the plain search misses
Prepare a complete pre-filing search report with a risk opinion a client can act on
Run dilution, proprietor and WIPO Global Brand Database searches, and know when transborder reputation matters
Read a Registry examination report in minutes and choose the right route for each objection
Draft a response to a Section 9 or Section 11 objection with the evidence index to back it
Prepare written submissions and a hearing file that survive the hearing officer's questions
Keep a prosecution docket clean: deadlines, file hygiene and the records the Registry will ask for
about: Most trademark training starts at the examination report. This course starts earlier, where the real decisions are made: the search. Six of the ten sessions are about finding what is already on the Register and on the market, reading it under Sections 9, 11 and 17, and writing an opinion that tells the client whether to file, change the mark, or walk away.

The second half is prosecution proper. You read real Registry examination reports, choose the route for each objection, draft the response, and then prepare the written submission and hearing file for the matters that are not waived. Two sessions are pure demonstration: a search report and a response drafted live, start to finish, and a final walk-through of one mark from the first search to the hearing notice.

Every session is recorded, and the recordings stay open to you for two months from the date you register: long enough to work through all ten at a session a week with time to spare, and to return to the parts you need on a live matter. Ten practice exercises, one per session, come with model answers. Questions go by email and are answered by the people who teach the course. Enrolling also places you in the VIDIKSHA community of IP professionals, where practitioners compare notes on real objections and Registry practice.

You also receive the IP Prosecution Kit at your doorstep: the Vidiksha Trademark Prosecution in Practice book, the prosecution and filing checklists, and the sample drafts the course is built around, printed, so they are on your desk when a real examination report lands.

faq.q: Are the sessions live or recorded?
faq.a: Recorded. All ten sessions are available from the day you enrol, so you can watch at your own pace and go back to a session when a live matter needs it. Questions go by email and are answered by the instructors.

faq.q: How long do I have access to the recordings?
faq.a: Two months from the date of registration. That is comfortably enough for the ten sessions and the exercises; if you need longer for a good reason, write to us before the period ends.

faq.q: What is in the IP Prosecution Kit, and how does it reach me?
faq.a: The Vidiksha Trademark Prosecution in Practice book, the prosecution checklist, the checklist for filing a trademark, and printed sample drafts for examination report responses, written submissions, and Section 9, Section 11 and common-law clearances. It is couriered to the address you give at registration, within India.

A private group of VIDIKSHA members who practise IP: associates, in-house counsel, agents and founders. It is where people compare notes on real objections, hearing experiences and Registry practice, and where we post updates when practice changes.

faq.q: Which Registry practice does this follow?
faq.a: Indian practice under the Trade Marks Act, 1999 and the Trade Marks Rules, 2017, as applied by the Registry today. Sessions are re-recorded when practice changes.
